finding: The added in-page diagnostic fetch()es a RequirePermissions<(RuntimeVersionRead,)> endpoint with only an Accept header. Access-token auth is Authorization: Bearer only (no cookie fallback; the refresh cookie is Path=/api/auth), so diag.status is 401, catalog is null, and the block throws UNCONDITIONALLY — turning a passing acceptance test into a permanent failure whose message misattributes the cause. Exactly the misdiagnosis it was added to prevent.

`credential` is initialised to Used from token.is_some() and only ever downgraded. If every attempt fails at the transport layer (DNS/refused/timeout) or returns 5xx/404, GitHub never validated the credential, yet the response reports credential_status="used" — documented as 'GitHub ACCEPTED it — 5000/hour'. A value asserted for the accepted case is reachable in the never-answered case.

Secondary-rate-limit detection is `retry-after` presence only. GitHub documents that a secondary rate limit may be returned WITHOUT retry-after, and such a response carries a NON-ZERO x-ratelimit-remaining — so both guards miss it and a bare 403 is classified as a rejection. That spends the scarce anonymous 60/hr/IP budget AND tells the operator to replace a perfectly valid token.

The fast cache path echoes the stored credential_status for the whole TTL (default 3600s, admin-settable to 86400s) and there is no production cache-bypass, so after an operator fixes the token the present-tense notice can persist for up to a day; symmetrically a newly-bad token stays invisible for the same window.

get_latest_version does `let response = result?;` before the status check, so on the transport-error path (rejection observed, then the anonymous re-issue fails at the network) the credential verdict is dropped and failure_note() is never appended — on exactly the failure the doc says the operator most needs explained.

CORROBORATES the correctness finding: the added pre-check fetches a permission-gated endpoint with no Authorization header, so it 401s and throws unconditionally BEFORE the (unchanged) row assertions, which are now dead code. Every other in-page fetch in this suite first reads the token out of localStorage['auth-storage'].

Even authenticated, the spec asserts NOTHING about the feature: credential_status appears only inside an error-message template, never in an expect. Mutation that survives: remove the is_auth_rejection fallback block entirely.

classification_ignores_token_shape_and_no_shape_filter_exists mutates process-global GITHUB_TOKEN WITHOUT taking ENV_LOCK — the mutex this module declares for exactly that, and which both pre-existing env-mutating tests take. It races them: its `prior` capture can pick up another test's temporary value and restore it permanently.

…and the same test is hollow: leg (a) re-runs assertions already made by its sibling, and its claimed property ('same verdict whatever credential') is a type-level fact since no credential is passed in — a phantom leg. Leg (b) duplicates the pre-existing github_token test.

failure_note() is interpolated at BOTH failing-read sites and NO test executes either interpolation with a Rejected credential. Mutation that survives the entire suite: replace both call sites with "". The only integration assertion about it is a NEGATIVE one, which a deletion also satisfies.

No AuthBehavior rejects BOTH the authenticated and the anonymous request, so the terminating path is untested. Mutation that survives: delete the anonymous_retries < ANONYMOUS_RETRY_LIMIT guard — the rescued case exits anyway because the second request succeeds.
/versions/available is asserted only for "rejected" — no used/absent control on that endpoint, so hardcoding credential_status:"rejected" in binary_manager.rs passes every test.

The mock decides on header PRESENCE and never inspects the value, so no test distinguishes 'the configured token was sent' from 'some token was sent'. Mutation that survives: send a hardcoded literal instead of the configured token.

The store action's credential_status mapping — the SOLE wire between the new backend field and the new UI branch — is executed by no test (the vitest harness seeds the store directly). Mutation that survives every gate: delete those two lines; the notice can then never appear in the real app.

The transient-retry counter was restructured and no test exercises the transient path. Mutation that survives: revert `attempt` to 0, which makes 2u64.pow(attempt-1) underflow and PANIC in debug on the first transient failure.
The transient+fallback interaction is untested and the worst case (4 upstream requests) exceeds the MAX_ATTEMPTS:3 contract without saying so.
The outage half simulates GitHub being down with abort() + a bare 200ms sleep and never verifies the port stopped accepting — a timing-dependent flake on a busy box.

The combined-state test hand-writes an unavailable_reason containing the production failure_note text but never asserts any of it is rendered, creating the appearance of covering the note pipeline while asserting nothing about it.
Nothing in the unit tier proves the classifier is WIRED into github_get_with_retry; the 403-rejection branch has no integration coverage at all.

SELF-FOUND while fixing the above: the new store test was first written as `*.credential.test.ts`, which vitest.config.ts's include (`src/**/*.store.test.ts`, `src/**/*.test.tsx`) does not match — the file was silently NEVER COLLECTED, and the mutation it was written to kill passed. Renamed to *.store.test.ts and re-verified by mutation.
